subject.title: [Bug]: Windows gateway listens but local health/status time out after Telegram polling stall (v2026.5.20)

question: Should repeated unrecovered Telegram or channel stalls escalate to Gateway process/supervisor recovery, or should OpenClaw require a fresh affected-host repro before changing that recovery boundary?
rationale: Current code intentionally gives up channel restarts in-process, while the reported user-visible failure is process-level unresponsiveness; changing that boundary affects active sessions and operator expectations.

options.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-main Windows affected-host health/status/Telegram proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

options.title: Add Supervised Recovery Policy
options.body: Define a bounded Gateway watchdog or process-exit policy for unrecovered stalls, with Windows and Linux service proof plus upgrade notes.

options.title: Stay Channel-Scoped
options.body: Continue fixing narrower Telegram transport and session bugs without adding process-level recovery unless a fresh repro proves it is necessary.

recommendation.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-main Windows affected-host health/status/Telegram proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

likelyOwner.reason: They already ran the targeted repro attempt and have recent merged history in the Telegram polling watchdog area most relevant to the remaining proof and policy gap.
